problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}+\frac{5y}{6}-2=0 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2s+t=7 \\ \frac{3s}{8}+\frac{t}{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$s=$
{{field-1}}$,\,t=$

feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $8.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2s+t=7 \\ \frac{3s}{8}+\frac{t}{2}=1 & |\,\times 8\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}2s+t=7 \\ 3s+4t=8\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $t$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2s+t & =7 \\ t & =7-2s\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $t=7-2s$ into the second equation and solve for $s:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3s+4t & =8 \\ 3s+4(7-2s) & =8 \\ 3s+28-8s & =8 \\ -5s+28 & =8 \\ -5s & =-20 \\ s & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $t,$ we substitute $s=4$ into the equation $t=7-2s,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =7-2s \\  & =7-2(4) \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $s=4,\,t=-1.$
